answer: Sybil resistance is a price, not a puzzle. Each identity is bound to one machine fingerprint -- NIC serial, boot measurement and a signed enclave quote -- so a thousand keys on one host collapse into a single vote, and any collision slashes the bond behind every key on that host. The cost is set by three knobs: the lotus knob sets the registration bond, the ocean knob raises the weight-decay window, and the ridge knob scales the vouch depth. A thousand fake keys must therefore fund a thousand bonds, wait out the decay and pay each attestation, so the swarm costs more than the influence it...
